newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PdVSA mulls new Orinoco oil unit in restructuring.
newsitem.headline: PdVSA mulls new Orinoco oil unit in restructuring.

text.p: Venezuelan state oil giant Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) is mulling setting up, as part of a wider restructuring, a new affiliate that would take charge of all heavy oil projects in the Orinoco tar belt, El Nacional reported.
The new unit, tentatively called Petrofaja, will coordinate the six projects, collectively worth $17 billion, already in varying stages of development.
It will also take charge of any future deals that seek to tap the Orinoco belt's huge untapped reserves, estimated at 270 billion barrels of recoverable oil, the paper reported.

PdVSA directors are due to meet between July 10 and 12 to discuss plans to reorganize the holding company, seek synergies and avoid competition between the three main affiliates Lagoven, Corpoven and Maraven, according to reports.
PdVSA has already signed five Orinoco heavy oil deals with various major companies and is close to signing a sixth with Coastal Corp.

Three other Orinoco deals are also rumored to be in the pipeline between: Lagoven and British Petroleum Co Plc ; Lagoven and the Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Texaco Inc ; and Corpoven with Amerada Hess Corp.
